texts.preamble: Sh. Trilok Yadav S/O Sh. Dukhaa Yadav vs Food Safety Officer on 18 December, 2019 In The Court Of Sh. Yashwant Kumar District & Sessions Judge/Fsat, New Delhi In the matter of : Fsat No. 14/19 (Cnr No. Dlnd010063782019) Sh. Trilok Yadav S/o Sh. Dukhaa Yadav R/o Shop No. 407, Phatakwali Gali VillageBhorgarh, Delhi40. ..... Appellant Versus Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan,Connaught Place New Delhi110001. .... Respondent Appeal Against The Order Dated 23.08.2018 Of Ld. Adjudicating Officer / Additional District Magistrate (North), Alipur, Delhi. Date of filing of appeal : 04.04.2019 Date of arguments : 17.12.2019 Date of judgment : 18.12.2019 J U D G M E N T :
texts.facts: Briefly stating, the facts as per the appeal are that appellant is running a shop under the name & style of M/s Yadav Misthan Bhandar at Shop No. 407, Phatakwali Gali,Village Bhorgarh, Delhi40. On 28.04.2016, a sample of "Milk Cake" was lifted by the Food Safety Officer (in short FSO) from the aforesaid premises where the sampled commodity was found stored for sale and the appellant was found vending the sampled commodity at the time of taking the sample. On analysis, the Food Analyst, Delhi, vide its report dated 04.05.2016, opined the said sample to be containing extraneous matter viz. added vegetable oil and added starch in contravention of Section 26(2)(ii) read with the definition of extraneous matter as defined under Section 3(1)(i) of the FSS Act. Consequently, a Sh. Trilok Yadav S/O Sh. Dukhaa Yadav vs Food Safety Officer on 18 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65545514/ 1 complaint was filed against the appellantherein by the FSO before the Adjudicating Officer. The appellant is running only a Tea shop from the said premises and not indulging in making any kind of sweets in his shop. Appellant used to sell sweets only after purchasing the same from other shop namely Jain Sweets, Narela, Delhi40. Appellant was not afforded with fair opportunity to put his defence before the Ld. ADM as he was directly served with the recovery notices dated 01.11.2018 & 01.03.2019. The Ld. ADM deliberately not served the appellant with the impugned order dated 23.08.2018. The proceedings conducted before the Ld. ADM is without the principle of natural justice as no opportunity of hearing was granted to the appellant. 4. The Ld. Chief PP for the State has not filed reply to the appeal, however, he has opposed the appeal. No notice was given to the appellant. On 17.04.2018, the appellant appeared and filed reply to FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 3 of 9 the said notice. On the same day i.e. on 17.04.2018, he was informed about the passing of the impugned order. Sweets were packed and not opened. Nothing is brought on record that the appellant was preparing the sweets from the shop. The Ld. ADM directly sent him with the recovery notices dated 01.11.2018 & 01.03.2019.
texts.arguments: 3. The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 2 of 9 alia on the grounds among others that the appellant has not been granted sufficient time to represent his case before the Ld. ADM. 6. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that impugned order in this case was passed on 23.08.2018 whereas the appellant has received the notice on 01.04.2019. The Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor argued that the appellant was having full opportunity to lead evidence but he did not appear before the Ld. ADM. The appellant endorsed that the sampled commodity was prepared at his shop. The appellant nowhere denied that the sampled commodity does not belong to him. Appellant is the owner of the said shop i.e. M/s Yadav Misthan Bhandar and was found selling the sampled commodity containing extraneous matter as per the report of Food Analyst, therefore, he is liable as per Section 27 of FSS Act. The appellant did not comply with the standards of rules / regulations of Food Safety and Standard Act. The impugned order has been rightly passed by the Ld.ADM. The Ld. Chief PP for the State, in support of his arguments, relied upon the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar versus The State of Uttar FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 4 of 9 Pradesh in Criminal Appeal No. 1541 of 2019 decided on 04.10.2019 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. 10. Section 3(1)(i) FSS Act defines "extraneous matter". It reads as under : Section 3 : Definition (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires .... (i) "extraneous matter" means any matter contained in an article of FSAT No. 14/19 Sh. Trilok Yadav vs. FSO Page No. 5 of 9 food which may be carried from the raw materials, packaging materials or process systems used for its manufacture or which is added to it, but such matter does not render such article of food unsafe; 11. 12. Section 26(2)(ii) FSS Act casts a responsibility on FBO not to manufacture, store, sell or distribute food article containing extraneous matter. Said provision reads as under: 26.Responsibilities of the Food business operator. .... (2) No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food - ..... (ii)which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter; or" 13. Section 27(1) FSS Act fastens liability for sale etc. of food article upon the manufacture or packer.
